the synthesis of new heterobimetallic porphyrins and their characterization by X-ray crystallography, electrochemistry, spectroscopy, and magnetic susceptibility measurements.
the development of synthetic strategies for heterobimetallic μ-nitrido porphyrins and their application to electrochemistry.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the FeIV=N═RuV and OsIV=N═RuIV bonding descriptions are more likely for the μ-nitrido porphyrins than the FeIV=N=RuIV and OsIV=N=OsIV descriptions, and the latter is not a likely description for the FeIV=N=OsV bonding.
the Fe(IV) and Os(IV) porphyrins are more stable toward oxidation than the Ru(IV) analogues.
the reaction of the nitrido complexes of 1 with the metalloporphyrin complexes of iron, ruthenium, and osmium leads to the formation of a variety of heterobimetallic μ-nitrido metalloporphirins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

heterobimetallic Fe/Ru μ-N complexes can be prepared from the reaction of FeIII porphyrins with [Ru(LOET)(N)Cl3] or [Ru(N)Cl2], but the Fe/Os analogues are not obtained from the reaction of the FeIII porphyriins with the corresponding Os(VI) nitrides.
heterobimetallic μ-nitrido porphyrins can be prepared by the reaction of a metalloporphyrin with a metal nitride complex.
heterobimetallic μ-nitrido metalloporphyrin complexes are accessible from the reactions of trans-[MII(TPP)(py)(CO)(OH2)] with [M'(LOEt)(N)(Cl)2].
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to prepare heterobimetallic complexes in which one of the metal atoms is in the +IV oxidation state.
the μ-nitrido bond is very stable in these heterobimetallic complexes, and that it can serve as a bridge for the formation of heterobimetalloporphyrin complexes.
the μ-nitride complexes of Fe/Ru (1), Fe/Os (1), and Os/Ru are stable in the solid state, and the Fe/Ru complex can be synthesized from FeII porphyrin.
